findings.summary: Isha's label is anchored on the Fajr ring's eastern half, which the half-arc change stopped drawing, so for interval-based methods the label floats with no line under it
'east'/'west' side naming is inverted relative to the usual convention and the test locks it in

note: 1/2 real. The Isha finding's mechanism is right but its stated consequence is wrong: side=1 is the evening side, so the label is on the correct half, it simply has no line beneath it any more. The naming finding is wrong outright - the sub-solar point tracks westward, so longitudes east of the noon meridian have already passed noon; code, comment and test all agree that east is afternoon. Two earlier attempts at this same review returned EMPTY with finish_reason=length after burning 32000 and then 64000 reasoning tokens on an 89k-char prompt; 64000 is the API ceiling, so ds-review.mjs now disables thinking by default.

findings.summary: HomeGlobeScreen rebuilds its data object every render, so SceneHost's effect and computeApplyKey run on every compass tick
updateGroundView re-arms the idle timer on every compass reading
Base3D.facing() allocates two Vector3 per call
Base3D.normalizeSprites allocates one Vector3 per frame
onCanvasPointerMove allocates two Quaternions and two Vector3 per pointermove while dragging the moon
HomeGlobeScreen's layout effect runs at compass rate

note: 0/6 actionable today. The two High findings and the layout-effect one all depend on the compass firing at 10-50Hz, but ground view's toggle is commented out in HomeGlobeScreen, so deviceHeading never changes and none of that path runs. The model could not see that the feature is switched off. facing() is only reached from sunDome, which is also commented out of App. The remaining allocations are one per frame or bounded by a drag. Its 'already optimal' list (loop parking, the applyKey guard, scratch-vector discipline, the loading-manager Set, dispose coverage) was accurate on every point I checked.

findings.summary: usePrayerTimes' refreshedForMs guard is never reset, so a refresh that lands before the boundary permanently disables the watchdog
ThemeContext runs a 60s interval for the life of the app regardless of whether the theme is 'auto'
App's updatePrayerTimes effect depends on the prayers array identity
TravelContext's expiry effect depends on the whole travel object
TravelContext's home-arrival effect recomputes a haversine on every travel-settings write
useQibla's startListening identity churns on location change

note: Best of the four perf reviews. H-2 is the clearest live waste in the whole assessment and is fixed. H-1 is real but its trigger is narrower than described: setTimeout cannot fire before its deadline, so the reachable path is a backward system-clock step while a boundary timer is pending, not ordinary early firing. The three Medium identity-dependency findings are all accurate and all cost a handful of operations per user action; left alone deliberately. M-4 talks itself out of its own finding mid-paragraph. Its 'already optimal' list was accurate.

findings.summary: An identical <style> keyframes block is emitted per table row, per render
A 60s tick at the table root re-renders the whole table and every row to refresh one boolean
Tracking status is loaded with five serial awaits
The tracking-status effect keys on the prayers array identity
CitySearch scans the full 33k city list once per popular name on every empty query
SunDomeCard's data memo rebuilds marks on every minute tick

note: 2/6 fixed. The <style> finding is overstated: React keeps a text node whose string is unchanged, so there is no per-render stylesheet re-parse - it is duplication, not repeated work. The 60s table tick is real but rebuilds a 5-8 row list once a minute, which measured as nothing. The prayers-identity effect fires once per prayer-times recompute (a few times a day), not per render as feared, because usePrayerTimes memoises. SunDomeCard is commented out of App. The city-search scan is 16 x 33,203 comparisons on opening the search and is fixed. Its restraint was good: it explicitly labelled several findings as too small to act on rather than inflating them.

findings.summary: The 4096x2048 coastline rasterisation blocks the main thread and re-runs on every theme change
qiblaGlobe's fadeLabelsNearTheEdge clones a Vector3 per frame
sunDome's separateLabels and anchorAwayFromEdge allocate a Vector3 per sprite per frame in a view that never parks
getCalculationParameters rebuilds a 12-entry table of closures on every call
scheduleNotifications recalculates seven days of prayer times per call
Every prayer-tracking read re-fetches and re-parses the whole stored blob
moonIllumination and subLunarPoint each recompute the lunar series, so a caller needing both pays twice

note: 4/7 fixed, the strongest yield of the four. The coastline finding is the headline of the whole assessment and its size estimate was right: measured 269ms of raster plus 163-193ms of ring decode at 4x CPU throttle, over 1421 rings and 60,629 vertices. The moon finding is wrong: moonIllumination has no caller anywhere in the app, and the model hedged it as a question rather than asserting it. sunDome is commented out of App. The seven-day notification recompute is deliberate and already narrowed to a settings subset.
